comments.text: Q&A: The dangers of rip currents on the Great Lakes and how to swim to safety Nathan MacIntyre has made it his life's mission to teach people about water safety on the Great Lakes. He joined London Morning host Andrew Brown to talk about what do if you get swept out to deep water by a rip current.
Longshore Currents paired with Structural Currents are deadly! ¡Las corrientes paralelas a la costa en conjunto con las corrientes estructurales pueden ser mortales!
Currents develop by several factors. It is best to be familiar with the different currents and why they develop so that you know what to expect before deciding whether to go to the beach or not.
National Safe Boating Week begins by discussing Marine Forecasts. The Great Lakes Marine Portal (weather.gov/greatlakes/) has plenty of information including current observations and forecasts.

Beach Safety: Do you know how to escape a dangerous current? Flip on your back, float, and follow the current or the safest path out of the water! For more info visit: dangerouscurrents.org weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…

Beach Safety: Learn about the other types of currents! Outlet, Channel, Longshore, and Structural Currents. The steps to get to safety vary depending on the type of current! weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…

Beach Safety: When trying to spot rip currents look for a muddy/sandy color in the water moving out into the lake. Also look for a break or ‘calm spot’ in between incoming waves. weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…

Beach Safety: Rip Currents are powerful currents of water moving away from shore. They can sweep even the strongest swimmer away. It's important to know what to do if caught in one! weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…

Beach Safety: There are certain conditions and locations prone to currents. Tomorrow we'll discuss the types of currents, how to avoid them and what to do if caught in one. weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…

Beach Safety: Designate a water watcher, an adult whose sole responsibility is to monitor swimmers in the water. Drowning is silent, learn what signs to watch for. weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…
Beach Safety: Be cautious in cold water. Cold water shock and hypothermia are real threats on the Great Lakes. For more information, visit weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…
When a high swim risk is expected a Beach Hazard Statement is issued to alert swimmers about life-threatening conditions on the lake. Visit: weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…

Know the swim risk before you head to the beach. Check the beach forecast BEFORE heading to a Great Lakes beach. For beach forecasts and beach hazards statements, visit weather.gov/lot/beachprepare weather.gov/lot/beachprepare…
